corrected_value.title: Intestinal dysbiosis and bacterial enteroinvasion in a murine model of Hirschsprung’s disease.

decisions.location: Introduction, lines 188-194; Discussion, lines 537-539, 562-564, 586-589; References, lines 1732-1754
decisions.quote:
Previous work using murine models of HSCR and HAEC revealed intestinal dysbiosis associated with aganglionosis, indicating a potential role for intestinal microbiomes in the promotion of HAEC (
Ward et al., 2012
;
Pierre et al., 2014
). We examined the reproducibility of these findings and also investigated the contribution of inter-facility effects to microbiome variability in C57BL/6J mice, reproducing the findings of
Rausch et al. (2016)
on a smaller scale.
decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. In the Introduction, the authors explicitly state that they examined the reproducibility of the intestinal dysbiosis findings in murine models of HSCR and HAEC reported by both Ward et al. (2012) and Pierre et al. (2014). In the Discussion, they directly compare their empirical genotype-based (KO vs. WT) taxonomic differences in Ednrb mice against the findings of Pierre et al. (2014) across multiple taxa, including enrichment of Enterobacteriaceae/Proteobacteria in Laramie KO mice, higher abundance of Bacteroides in KO mice, and lower abundance of Lactobacillus in diseased versus healthy mice. Reference lines 1732-1754 identify Pierre et al. (2014) (10.1016/j.jpedsurg.2014.01.060, J. Pediatr. Surg. 49, 1242-1251), which is an independent original study from a different research group rather than an alternate report of shipped row 938 (Ward; Pieretti; Dowd; Cox; Goldstein, 2012, 10.1111/j.1365-2982.2012.01937.x) or of sibling target_index 2 (Rausch et al., 2016).

decisions.quote:
Previous work using murine models of HSCR and HAEC revealed intestinal dysbiosis associated with aganglionosis, indicating a potential role for intestinal microbiomes in the promotion of HAEC (
Ward et al., 2012
;
Pierre et al., 2014
). We examined the reproducibility of these findings and also investigated the contribution of inter-facility effects to microbiome variability in C57BL/6J mice, reproducing the findings of

decisions.reason: No prior adjudication or state file exists for this work. Beyond testing the Ednrb disease model, the authors conducted a dedicated empirical sub-study of fecal microbiomes in normal C57BL/6J mice across two facilities (n = 10 mice per facility in Boston and Laramie) explicitly 'reproducing the findings of Rausch et al. (2016) on a smaller scale,' testing inter-facility PERMANOVA UniFrac differences, core microbiome conservation, and alpha diversity (Results lines 445-479) and concluding in the Discussion that 'Our findings in C57BL/6J mice are consistent with a previous report ( Rausch et al., 2016 ).' Reference lines 1784-1806 identify Rausch et al. (2016) (10.1016/j.ijmm.2016.03.004, Int. J. Med. Microbiol. 306, 343-355), which is completely distinct from shipped row 938 (Ward et al., 2012, 10.1111/j.1365-2982.2012.01937.x) and from sibling target_index 1 (Pierre et al., 2014, 10.1016/j.jpedsurg.2014.01.060).
